previousHostControl.note: The same bundle runs on the host that registers no NativeIdleCallbacksCxx: the idle callbacks are lazy getters, so the bundle evaluates, the root mounts and queueMicrotask and setImmediate work, and the first read of requestIdleCallback or cancelIdleCallback fails. It fails exactly the checks that need the new module, and holds the five that need only the JS the bundle runs (the flag, the globals before the bundle and the lazy getters, RN's immediateShim, setImmediate over the microtask module) and the lifecycle and report checks. Its native producers are pinned for the tree; the old binary was built from executionBaseCommit.

retainedSabotage.mechanism: set-up-timers-not-imported, timeout-ignored, reimplemented, cancel-dropped, gate-removed and window-open are in-memory esbuild overrides (scripts/idle-callbacks-bundle.mjs), no file is edited; no-module, strict-ignored and strict-waits-for-teardown break one line of native/application_runtime.cpp, rebuild the host, keep it in the variant's hostDirectory and restore the source byte for byte (scripts/sabotage-sources.mjs)

oracle.independence: Written from RN's pinned sources, not from the probe: what setUpTimers' bridgeless branch installs and from where, the spec and C++ of the NativeIdleCallbacks module (the 50 ms deadline, the timeout that only drives didTimeout and never reaches the scheduler, the timeRemaining rules, the handle, the cancel), and the RuntimeScheduler's priority timeouts, the idle task's default timeout, the smallest expiration first, the yield, the cancel and the checkpoint after each task are read from the files; the order of each case and what each idle callback is told are derived by a model of the host's event loop whose scheduler is the C++ one over a virtual clock that only a spin advances and whose microtask queue is V8's own (Promise reactions, queueMicrotask and RN's immediateShim run in a vm context); a reading of timeRemaining is judged against the timestamps the report carries and the 50 ms of the source; every verdict of the probe is derived again from the report's raw observations.

limits: The cases are the handler of a Pressable's onPress in one headless root; the order of idle callbacks against other work is certified for work queued from inside a RuntimeScheduler task.
The timer cases depend on the host taking a timer registered in a handler in a later pump than the RuntimeScheduler's loop; the oracle reads that order from native/application_runtime.cpp.

The readings of timeRemaining are bounded by the timestamps of the lane, not fixed: the deadline is measured from a time the C++ takes, which the report brackets between the request and the callback's entry.
The gate is the host's extension (V2-D27); callback exceptions, setImmediate under load and a Promise storm are slice F's.
The registry counts the calls that reach RN's module in front of RN's own invokers; the module's C++ is compiled unchanged.
The headless desktop host only; no mobile export has run this bundle.
Hosted CI is pending: the record is of the local run.
